profiles.name: House hygiene - uncited on purpose
profiles.description:
Rules a firewall team might agree among themselves. None of them cites an external standard, and the report says so on every line: `cited: false`, and the summary counts them.
That labelling is the point. A house rule is a perfectly good reason to fix something - it is not a reason to tell an auditor the estate is non-compliant with a standard. Keeping the two visibly apart is what makes the rest of the report worth reading.

profiles.name: NIST SP 800-41 Rev. 1 - the configuration-checkable part
profiles.description:
A starting point, not an authority. Every check below cites the clause it comes from, so a reader who disagrees can argue with NIST rather than with this tool. Copy this file, delete what does not apply to your estate, and add your own - that is the point of the format.
Read `not_checkable` at the bottom before presenting a clean run: several of the publication's most important recommendations are process controls that no configuration reader can verify.

notes: Profiles are files, not code. Copy one, edit it, and it is yours.
A check with no cited standard still runs; it is reported as a house rule so nobody mistakes it for a regulatory finding.
